draft.title: Limiting reactants
card: the reactant that runs out first. The reaction stops when it is gone, so it sets how much product can form.
a reactant that is left over when the reaction stops.

Reactants combine in the ratio in the balanced equation. To find the limiting reactant, change each amount to moles and compare. In CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, 1 mol of CH4 needs 2 mol of O2, so if there is less O2 than that, O2 is limiting.
Then use the moles of the limiting reactant and the equation's ratio to find the product. Here 2 mol of O2 makes 1 mol of CO2, so 1 mol of O2 makes 0.5 mol of CO2.
draft.remember: Find which reactant runs out first, then use its moles and the ratio to find the product.

a.q: A reaction stops because one reactant is all used up. Some of the other reactant is still there. What does the leftover reactant tell you?
opts: It is in excess, and the used up reactant was limiting
It is limiting, and the used up reactant was in excess
Both reactants were present in the exact ratio
The reaction did not follow the balanced equation
a.why: The reaction stops when one reactant runs out, so that one is the limiting reactant. The reactant left over is in excess. It did not stop the reaction, so it is not limiting.
a.clue: Which reactant ran out and stopped the reaction?

b.q: Methane burns: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. A container holds 3 mol of CH4 and 2 mol of O2. Which statement is correct?
opts: O2 is limiting, and 2 mol of H2O can form
CH4 is limiting, and 6 mol of H2O can form
O2 is limiting, and 1 mol of H2O can form
CH4 is in excess, and 6 mol of H2O can form
b.why: 3 mol of CH4 would need 6 mol of O2, but there is only 2 mol, so O2 runs out first and is limiting. The product comes from the limiting reactant: O2 to H2O is 2 to 2, so 2 mol of H2O forms. Using the 3 mol of CH4 to get 6 mol of H2O is wrong, because CH4 is in excess and not all of it reacts.
b.clue: Work out the product from the reactant that runs out first.

a.best: It is in excess, and the used up reactant was limiting

b.best: O2 is limiting, and 2 mol of H2O can form
